features.feature_value: Decision hinged on distinguishing political opinions from insults/dehumanizing/hostile language; kept when both sides were opinion-only, omitted when both were hostile/insulting.
features.evidence_span: distinction between political opinion and insults or dehumanizing and hostile language
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes a keep/omit rule based on whether language is opinion versus hostile/dehumanizing.

features.feature_value: Chose not to moderate most content; would only remove when someone threatens or possibly breaks the law, viewing censorship as harmful.
features.evidence_span: Unless someone is threatening someone or possibly breaking the law
features.rationale: Their criteria specify a high threshold for removal (threats/lawbreaking) and a general bias against moderation.

features.feature_value: Sought to remove excessive vulgar language and anything promoting violence, while feeling that disagreement should generally be allowed.
features.evidence_span: Excessive vulgar language, anything promoting violence. Essentially no matter how much I disagree
features.rationale: They state a specific content-based target (vulgarity/violence) paired with an explicit exception for disagreement.

features.feature_value: Looked for direct threats/inciting violence but found less than expected; still generally viewed content as acceptable for political discussion despite being depressing/unintelligent.
features.evidence_span: expecting more direct threats and inciting violence, but thankfully it wasn't present
features.rationale: They describe assessing severity by checking for threats/incitement and adjusting their moderation decision accordingly.

features.feature_value: Removed emotional/inflammatory posts; kept posts grounded in reality/parties’ opinions and not just propaganda.
features.evidence_span: remove posts that were emotional and inflammatory. I kept posts that seemed grounded in reality
features.rationale: Their reflections attribute influence to perceived tone (emotional/inflammatory) and framing quality (realistic vs propaganda).

features.feature_value: Assessed social-media posts by anticipating negative/positive impact and viewed profanity as not always useful in conversation; leaned toward positivity.
features.evidence_span: Using profanity is not always useful in a conversation
features.rationale: They connect moderation with a conversational-impact evaluation that specifically mentions profanity.

features.feature_value: Rejected only when it didn’t add to a healthy, positive discussion; otherwise kept based on having merit and not wanting to be disrespectful.
features.evidence_span: Plus I dont want to be disrespectful
features.rationale: They justify keep/remove using a norm of respectful tone and the perceived value for healthy discussion.

features.feature_value: Rejected when some pairs seemed too similar or didn’t make sense at all.
features.evidence_span: too similar or didnt make sense at all
features.rationale: They describe a structural/consistency sanity check on the paired items that informed rejection.
